decisions.reason: The required $10-to-$20 coded-referral commission copy change is already represented by the candidate's same-message MODIFY.
The active About-page content describes coded-referral earnings using the prior $10 amount, so the confirmed $20 coded-referral commission necessarily requires corresponding copy consistency.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
At this point, 34 mints should correspond to 34 tickets and 34 x $20 commissions.

A mint still produces a ticket and commission even when no referral code is supplied.

Accounting works correctly on the leaderboards and NFT attributes whenever a code is used. That part is perfect.

Without a referral code, the ticket and commission are assigned randomly, but both must still appear on the leaderboard and in the NFT attributes.

Since your latest fix, the randomly assigned tickets from the last 7 mints seem to have been recorded correctly, which is great. The earlier missing tickets have not been backfilled, though.

The $18 commissions generated by these no-code buys are also still missing from the leaderboard and NFT attributes.

My screenshot shows an NFT with 9 tickets but only 4 x $20 commissions. That should be impossible because every ticket comes with a $18 commission.

The leaderboard screenshot accounts for only 15 tickets and 12 x $8 commissions from 34 total mints. Regardless of whether a referral code was supplied, 34 mints should produce 34 tickets and 34 x $20 commissions.

value_updates.coded_referral_commission_copy: State that each eligible mint using a referral code pays an immediate, unlimited $20 commission to the referrer.

decisions.reason: The coded-referral commission copy change does not affect book-cover placement, size, cropping, or visibility.
The candidate already has a same-message MODIFY setting the coded-referral commission amount to $20.
The commission copy change does not alter email delivery, provider configuration, or the defined transactional-email contents.
The commission amount does not change the email authentication method or dashboard-access workflow.
The commission copy change does not affect the current or planned product name.

The source clearly establishes $20 for coded-referral commissions but gives conflicting $20, $18, and $8 figures when discussing no-referral accounting, so the no-referral commission amount cannot be propagated safely.
The source changes coded-referral commission copy but does not change the existing $900 prize amount, three-winner rule, 750-sale trigger, or prize-pool allocation.
The candidate already requires one ticket per eligible coded-referral mint, and the source reports that coded-referral ticket accounting works rather than changing that rule.

The candidate already requires randomly distributed commissions to appear in NFT attributes; the source reports missing historical and no-code accounting rather than establishing a new metadata value.
The commission copy change does not affect which book access, referral identity, badges, or prize tickets follow an NFT transfer.
